Per BSE's observations letter, public shareholders' interest would change from 50.11% in Shanti Educational Initiatives to 10.03% in GREW Energy after the scheme is implemented, and companies must disclose implications for their respective shareholders regarding rights and holding values. SEIL shares rose about 3% on the news; this figure is reported by the article rather than attributed as a verified market outcome.
items.title: BSE cleared SEIL's restructuring plan ahead of GREW Energy listing

items.summary: The Delhi High Court sought written responses from the Enforcement Directorate, Bureau of Immigration, and Serious Fraud Investigation Office regarding whether a look-out circular has been issued against Tina Ambani. Justice Mini Pushkarna issued notices after she filed a disclosure petition seeking confirmation on any LOC ahead of her planned departure for Thailand, the UAE, Oman, and Bhutan on December 10. Her counsel, Arshdeep Singh Khurana, told the court that no summonses were currently pending from either agency; he sought to have any existing LOC disclosed or its absence placed on record before she travels. In her petition, Ambani expressed concern that an SFIO LOC might stem from its investigation into Reliance Group companies or that an ED LOC could relate to a money-laundering probe under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. She cited summonses received in February by the ED and on July 20 under Section 217 of the Companies Act, 2013 by the SFIO, which she responded to through written communications and her lawyers; she also wrote to the Bureau of Immigration on August 28 seeking confirmation but reported receiving no response. She argued that being kept unaware of an LOC's existence would bar any legal challenge, characterizing this as a violation of natural justice and Articles 14, 19, and 21 of the Constitution. The underlying investigations concern loans exceeding ₹40,000 crore obtained by Anil Dhirubhai Ambani Group companies from public and private sector banks, with investigators suspecting diversion through complex financial transactions; the ED's probe also examines a suspected trail linked to a luxury condominium purchase in Manhattan. No LOC has been confirmed as existing—only that its status is being sought—and no response had been filed by any agency at the time of reporting.
items.title: Delhi HC seeks ED and SFIO responses on whether an LOC exists against Tina Ambani before her planned December travel abroad.

items.summary: The US Commission on International Religious Freedom alleged Thursday that India is targeting Muslim citizens during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls (SIR), removing them from voter lists, labeling them 'foreigners,' and deporting them. The commission's head Asif Mahmood attributed these claims to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who called three crore removed voters 'Bangladeshi infiltrators' on November 2 and referred to India's Muslims as 'infiltrators.' Commissioner Gene Mills characterized the expulsion of citizens based on Muslim faith as a religious-freedom escalation. The commission recommended that the US Department of State designate India a country of particular concern, though its suggestions are non-binding; it had made this recommendation in its 2026 annual report too. The Ministry of External Affairs has not responded but previously dismissed the panel's assessments as biased and politically motivated, while Indian ambassador Sharjeel Imam—detained over six years in an untried 2020 Delhi riots case—urged the commission to introspect its 'prejudices.' Separately, the SIR itself is contested: conducted across phases from Bihar (2025) through 19 states and Union Territories by mid-2026, it has drawn opposition claims of mass voter deletion, Supreme Court confirmation of legality without letting the Election Commission decide citizenship, BJP-state use of results to deny ration cards and passports, and nationwide protests since October 2 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.title: US religious freedom panel alleges India targets Muslims in electoral roll revision

items.summary: On November 19, the International Court of Justice ruled in Gambia v Myanmar that the Tatmadaw's attacks on the Rohingya met the legal definition of genocide under the 1948 UN Genocide Convention. The court found specific intent to destroy the group by concluding that the pattern, selective targeting and lethality of the attacks could not plausibly be explained as a counterinsurgency operation (at least 10,000 Rohingya are thought dead; roughly 750,000 fled to Bangladesh). The ruling is described as unprecedented in three ways: it found for the first time that a state committed genocide rather than merely failed to prevent it; it imposed obligations on Myanmar toward victims—reparations and compensation, safe voluntary return, restoration of citizenship after 1982 legislation rendered them stateless—and investigation into individual criminal responsibility (linking the case to the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant for Min Aung Hlaing and national universal-jurisdiction courts); and it accepted Gambia's "erga omnes partes" standing argument. The author attributes a key consequence: accepting that legal tool opens a pathway for other Genocide Convention cases, most significantly South Africa v Israel over alleged genocide against Palestinians in Gaza. Enforcement is limited because the ICJ has no enforcement arm; the Myanmar government cannot be compelled to comply, but reputational damage and support for sanctions, financial restrictions, arms-sale prohibitions and other cooperation limits are described as likely consequences (the author frames these as probable rather than certain). The article notes a weakened international legal environment over 20 years and an ICC "under siege by the Trump administration," presented as context. Judge Iwasawa Yuji read the judgment; thousands in Bangladeshi refugee camps reportedly chanted "Thank you Gambia."
items.title: ICJ finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya; ruling may shape Israel case

items.summary: Kolkata recorded roughly 35 mm of rainfall between 8:30 AM and 5:30 PM on Thursday as Cyclone Akvan's outer bands brought continuous rain, per The Telegraph. The India Meteorological Department issued a yellow watch for heavy rainfall over Kolkata and adjacent districts until 2 PM Friday, November 20, warning of thunderstorms with winds of 30-40 km/h and up to 7-11 cm of rain across six areas; IMD attributes the stronger impact on Bengal to Akvan's projected landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha being closer than previous cyclone landfalls. AccuWeather separately forecasts a maximum around 23 degrees Celsius, minimum 21 degrees Celsius, wind gusts up to 70 km/h, and roughly 9 mm of rain over 5.5 hours on Friday with a 91% precipitation probability; it projects heavier evening rainfall (13.7 mm) and overnight totals (13.4 mm). The Telegraph reports that South 24-Parganas, East Midnapore, West Midnapore, Jhargram and Bankura face very heavy rain warnings, with some areas possibly receiving up to 200 mm within 24 hours; AccuWeather instead forecasts only light rain on Saturday (rising to 27 degrees Celsius), sunshine Sunday (31 degrees Celsius), returning thunderstorms Monday November 23, and improved conditions Tuesday. The two sources disagree materially: IMD warns of heavy rainfall across six districts while AccuWeather's district-level forecast is limited to Kolkata with modest totals; the article presents Akvan's northward track as an established fact rather than a forecast, though it was described as expected landfall near Gopalpur.
items.title: Cyclone Akvan triggers yellow rain alert across Kolkata and neighbouring districts

items.summary: Pakistan Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik visited New Delhi for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum, drawing criticism from Congress and other opposition parties over his past threats toward India. The central government and Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat defended hosting him as consistent with multilateral protocol, noting that all member nations were invited to the cultural summit.
items.title: India hosts Pakistan's climate change minister at SCO civilisational forum amid opposition criticism

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur police arrested two accused and recovered jewellery, valuables, tools, and a motorcycle worth approximately Rs 45 lakh in the theft of Sanjeev Jain's residence at Mahavir Colony under Mandi police station. The complaint was registered on November 17 after gold and silver jewellery belonging to the daughter-in-law, along with cash and other items, went missing; SSP Abhinandan formed joint teams from Mandi police station, SOG, SWAT, and the surveillance cell. Two accused were arrested on November 19 following a tip-off near Baba Laladas Road: Chona alias Mujammil of Muzaffarnagar's Civil Lines area, with around seven criminal cases against him in Saharanpur and Muzaffarnagar, and Salim from Roorkee residing at Khata Khedi. Police attributed the 24-hour resolution to CCTV analysis and surveillance inputs rather than any single investigative method; they described the entry as jumping a boundary wall behind the property and entering the kitchen through an exhaust fan slot opening. SSP Abhinandan announced a Rs 25,000 cash reward for the joint teams involved.
items.title: Saharanpur police recover Rs 45 lakh stolen from jeweller within 24 hours

items.summary: Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai announced on Friday that Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra (Balen) Shah will undertake a state visit to India from November 22 to 23 at the invitation of Indian PM Narendra Modi. A 34-member government delegation led by Shah is scheduled to depart Kathmandu for New Delhi, with a delegation-level meeting between the two prime ministers set for Monday followed by joint project inaugurations in energy and bilateral cooperation agreements. The itinerary also includes a call on President Droupadi Murmu, wreath-laying at Rajghat's Mahatma Gandhi memorial, and attendance at the Nepal-India Business Forum. The visit is framed against India-Nepal ties rooted in historical bonds, the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, a 1,751-kilometre open border, and an adage describing shared livelihoods; these are described as evolving toward pragmatic economic, energy, and digital integration under Nepal's new leadership. The relationship framing is presented by the source rather than independently established.
items.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah to make state visit to India, November 22-23

items.summary: The White House named Department of War chief information officer Kirsten Davies as US national cyber director, replacing Sean Cairncross. The appointment comes against scrutiny over widespread service outages at Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, air traffic control and the National Security Agency that disrupted travel, bank access and classified communications; even Trump allies accused officials of withholding causes. Davies reportedly holds nearly two decades in cybersecurity after roles as Unilever's chief information security officer, plus positions at Estée Lauder, Barclays-Africa, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Siemens, and she founded the Institute for Cyber nonprofit. She became Department of War CIO on December 23, 2025, following Senate confirmation, advising the defence secretary on cyber matters while overseeing its strategy and budget. Accounts of Cairncross's departure conflict: Axios reported he declined another two-year term to allow time before Democrats take control in January, describing it as amicable, while CNN cited a White House source saying Trump supported firing him for lacking strong cyber credentials. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth welcomed the appointment, citing her dedication and confidence she would advance Trump's agenda; Trump dismissed the outages with "things like that happen," and Rubio said there was zero information linking them to a malicious actor. JPMorgan Chase attributed its incident to third-party providers targeted in a cyberattack, which Fox News linked to a ransomware group called Non-profit claiming responsibility for leaking data tied to JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard.
items.title: Trump names Kirsten Davies as national cyber director amid service outages

items.summary: Per a report by The Information, Meta intends to sell its pocket-sized Muse Charm AI device at $300 with up to 12 months of free 5G data from Verizon. These figures come from an unnamed source and are unconfirmed; Reuters could not immediately reach Verizon for comment, while a Meta spokesperson declined specifics but said the company would share more soon. The roughly two-inch (5-cm) device carries Muse, an AI agent unveiled in September by CEO Mark Zuckerberg that lets users delegate tasks such as shopping, travel booking and form-filling directly through taps on its screen without relying on smartphone apps. A built-in 5G modem enables access to Muse even without Wi-Fi, though the device cannot make calls. Meta frames the gadget as part of a broader effort to reduce dependence on Apple and Google operating systems by building its own AI platform. The launch is expected in time for December's holiday shopping season, according to Zuckerberg at Connect.
items.title: Meta plans $300 price and 12 months of free Verizon 5G for Muse Charm AI device

items.summary: Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar was reportedly admitted to a private hospital in Chennai on Wednesday night, with sources indicating he is likely to remain under medical observation for about two days. No official confirmation came from Lok Bhavan. DMK president MK Stalin spoke by phone to inquire about his health and wished him a speedy recovery, per a party release.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Governor Arlekar hospitalised; Stalin wishes recovery

items.summary: A tiger was seriously injured after a passing car hit it near Khatgaon Phata close to Sindewahi on the Nagpur highway in Maharashtra's Chandrapur district on Thursday around 10.15 am. Per Lokmat, Ashish Sudhakar Santoshwar of Ballarpur reported that the animal pounced on his two-wheeler while crossing the road before colliding with a car carrying him and family travelling from Nagbhid to Chandrapur; the driver reportedly stopped immediately after impact. A video circulating on social media shows the injured tiger lying in bushes beside the highway, with a gathered crowd allegedly making noises to provoke it as the animal bares its teeth but stays put without charging. The incident raised concerns about how people behave around vulnerable wild animals. After initial care at Savargaon, the tiger was shifted to the Transit Treatment Centre (TTC) in Chandrapur for further treatment.
items.title: Injured tiger struck by car near Khatgaon Phata, Chandrapur; onlookers reportedly provoking it
